description: We are building SonifySphere, an interactive NASA Earth Information Jukebox that pairs global temperature data with synchronized visuals and sound. We love NASA data, climate science, web development, data visualization, creative technology, and accessible storytelling. Join us to make science easier to understand. We welcome teammates skilled in coding, data analysis, UI/UX, audio, research, testing, and communications.
summary: SonifySphere is a full-stack, cross-platform web application, built with NextJS, Typescript, ToneJS, and Azure. It addresses the challenge of EIC data being primarily vision-oriented by turning EIC visual frames into a customizable audio output that maintains both detail and melody. It directly accesses NASA EIC Data: SVS 5101, DYAMOND CO2, Sea Surface Currents, GIBS, EPIC, EONET, POWER, and Image Library. The app is also compatible with Screen Readers, prioritizing low-vision users. Understanding the hassle of having to upload your own EIC data, we implemented a search feature that helps users find EIC data that they want to sonify. And as a final touch, we added educational games and made the design space-themed.
details: SonifySphere is a full-stack web application that takes NASA EIC visual frames and turns them into sound. The benefit is that it takes overtly visual data and sonifies it. This allows low-vision or no-vision users to be able to observe and analyze the data. It also reveals patterns in the data that might not have been easily seen, but rather easily heard. The overall intended impact is to make EIC data more accessible globally: Humans have 5 senses, but the strengths of those individual senses differ, which is why our app exists to bridge those differences. We used Codex and Grok for SI, and NextJS, Typescript, ToneJS, and Azure for the main tech stack. We made our project creative by adding features such as explorative sonification, where the user can move their cursor around a 2D representation of a globe to hear different sounds for different areas. We also added fun games to make it more friendly. The main factor we considered was UI/UX, specifically for low-vision users, since they are a part of our intended audience.
